title: Scalar Vector Runahead
problem: Graph and database applications have irregular memory accesses and low computation-to-communication ratios, making them memory-bound and unable to run efficiently on simple in-order cores despite their energy advantages. Prior Vector Runahead mechanisms are too complex and power-hungry for energy-efficient in-order processors.
motivation: Growing data privacy and edge computing demands require running analytics workloads on energy-efficient processors in edge devices like mobile phones.
method: SVR works by predicting which irregular memory addresses (addresses that don't follow a regular pattern) an in-order processor will need next. Instead of waiting for each memory access to complete before starting the next, SVR launches multiple temporary copies of these predicted accesses in parallel, each using a different predicted loop counter value (the numbers that typically control how many times a loop repeats). These parallel memory requests fetch data while the main program continues computing, hiding the stalls (waiting periods) that normally slow down simple processors. By overlapping independent memory accesses, SVR exposes memory-level parallelism (the ability to have many memory requests active simultaneously) even on simple in-order processors.
key_novelty: Using temporary parallel execution of predicted irregular memory accesses—each from a different predicted loop counter value—to extract memory parallelism on simple in-order processors.
contributions: Scalar Vector Runahead mechanism for memory-level parallelism extraction on in-order processors
Achieves 3.2x speedup over baseline in-order core with only 2 KiB hardware overhead
Outperforms full out-of-order cores (1.3x at 2 KiB, 1.7x at 9 KiB overhead) while reducing energy consumption by 50%
Enables efficient graph and database processing on energy-constrained edge devices

metrics.speedup: 3.2x vs 3-wide in-order core, 1.3x vs out-of-order (2 KiB), 1.7x vs out-of-order (9 KiB)

primary_theme: Memory-level parallelism for energy-efficient in-order cores
